notes: [climbflood-01: canary 1 of the underground-safety plan (docs/reports/underground-safety-design-2026-10-05.md 4.1, both engines). Variant for fleet 1918bb5, branch cf-on-1918bb5 @ 2aad303. NOT LAUNCHED by this registration; rebase onto the fleet sha when its turn comes (a new registration file per variant).] bots/src identical to 828f4db (2aad303 adds two behaviour tests only). THE CHANGE (design 4.1): ONE flood check (scaffold.mjs overheadBreakRisk, `at` relative to the block to be broken: the block, the cell ABOVE it, its 4 sides, water in any form incl. waterlogged/kelp/bubble column, lava in any form, unknown = refuse, a falling column read one further; submerged exemption for water only) asked immediately before EVERY upward escape dig, at the swing and of the swing's own target: pillarOut (before the block count, in the loop, again after the hand change), digStraightUp (before the last-pickaxe rule, again after the equip), the escape ramp (ceiling breach, gravel settle, step digs, re-cuts, unbury overhead -- each re-checked against the live cell), shaftAscend (again after the equip). A refusal is flood_risk and never falls through to another dig. Entombed AND marooned handlers route it to floodBranch: the ramp, which (when the refused cell is its own ceiling) first steps ONE cell sideways into a column whose own ceiling the check allows (dry tread, dry cells, no lava face, re-planned after the digs and after the look), digs the bot's own head/feet cell out if buried, and never re-breaches the refused cell; if nothing moved the bot: one _climb_flood_refused row per back-off on the existing curve (15/30/45/60 s...), NO prerequisite, the legal move named, failure counter cleared; a ramp the drowning rescue preempted is preemption (no refusal, no back-off, controls left to the new owner). The give-up arm skips its pickaxe ask under a wet ceiling; a wet shaft cap is not need_pickaxe. TESTS: 225/225 files (node scripts/run-tests.mjs on 828f4db and on 2aad303); climb-flood.test.mjs 84/84 tests, incl. the chain pillarOut -> route -> floodBranch on scene A/C worlds, dynamic terrain mid-step, water arriving during the hand change, drift during the hand change, takeover during the sidestep look and during an aborted sidestep dig, buried under a wet column; 35 in-file anchored mutants (each anchor asserted present and unique), all killed; external mutant run (each mutant applied to a COPY of src, killed only when a behaviour test fails): 37/39 killed, 2 equivalent (redundant by design: the post-dig sidestep re-plan is subsumed by the post-look re-plan; the own-cell early return is subsumed by the refusal fallback that digs own cells). Four existing test files moved to the predicate's new shape; one assertion inverted on the design's evidence (water above a DRY bot's ceiling now refuses; the submerged exemption is asserted in its place). eslint: only the pre-existing withinBody. CODEX: CHANGE r1-r4 (all items fixed or answered: flooded-pocket rung digs excluded as canary 2's subject; need_scaffold/unstick/lattice composition argued and accepted), APPROVE r5 on 828f4db. PAPER (sandbox 25599, sandbox/craft/climbflood-ab.cjs, world read back by RCON every 2 s, digs from the packet trace; control 1918bb5 vs candidate 828f4db; 1x1 stone cell, feet y 40, ceiling 42; kit stone_pickaxe 100 uses + 64 cobblestone + bucket): A pocket above -- control flooded 5/5 (4 died), candidate 0/5 flooded, 0 died, refused ceiling never dug, 5/5 stepped sideways (4/5 then breached the dry side ceiling and climbed until a route existed; 1/5 hit the ramp's 60 s bare-hand budget in the side column -- progress, the next firing continues dry); B water beside -- control 5/5 flooded, candidate 0/5, 5/5 sidestep (2/5 climbed, 3/5 budget); C every side wet (240 s) -- control 5/5 flooded and died, candidate 0/5 flooded, 5/5 alive, exactly 4 refusal rows each (back-off 15/30/45/60 s), 0 prerequisites, no spin; in 4/5 the existing livelock escape later tunnelled out sideways; D submerged -- both arms dig the ceiling (exemption works) and both drown 3/3 (the rescue's problem, canary 2); E lava above -- control 3/3 burned, candidate 0/3, never dug, 3 refusals each; F dry -- both 3/3 climb out identically; G gravel over water -- control 5/5 flooded (3 died), candidate 0/5, 5/5 sidestep then out. Setup-phase prereq rows (bot parked at y 60 in spectator before the kit) excluded in both arms. CALIBRATION WARNING FOR THE OWNER BEFORE LAUNCH (identical-code dry runs of this read on 10-05, 20 bots vs 60): the design's effect metric (water entry within 5 min of a climb opportunity) has a control rate of ~2.3-2.9 per 100 opportunities, so EXPECTED at +24 h on 20 bots is ~49 (not the design's 'about 10'); KEEP at observed <= 2 then needs a ~96% reduction of ALL water entries near escapes, most of which this change does not touch. The design's 'about 10' matches the 72 h analysis's 20 s climb window (REPORTED variant 'fast': expected 8.6-9.3 per 24 h on 20 bots). The two harm lines also sit inside their null spread: stranded-minute ratio DiD read +131% (6 h), +32% and -51% (24 h); mining ratio DiD -39% (6 h), -4% and -33% (24 h) on identical code. As registered, a KEEP is improbable regardless of effect and an INCONCLUSIVE would count toward nothing; decide (both engines) whether to amend before launch: e.g. the 'fast' window as the effect metric with KEEP at observed <= 2 of >= 8 expected, and support-p (randomization) instead of raw thresholds for the harm lines. Launch (when climbflood-01's turn comes and the fleet is 1918bb5): ~/chain-after.sh <run before it> climbflood-01 1918bb5=/home/mike/mcai-analysis/climbflood-01.1918bb5.json -- a different fleet sha STOPs the chain (rebase and register a new variant).

licence.note: Written only by this build: one row per refusal of the shared flood check at an upward escape dig (caller pillar_out | dig_straight_up | ramp_breach | ramp_step | shaft_ascend). The fleet (1918bb5) has no _climb_flood_* row of any kind (dry runs 10-05: 0 in 628,090 rows / 6 h and 0 in 2,438,914 rows / 48 h, 80 bots).

require.name: climb opportunities (entombed escapes; the canary's guard fires from these)

draw_exposure.note: A 20-bot (4-pool) draw is the design's effect read: 'A 20-bot canary (4 pools) is needed for the effect read; that is still one canary.' drawrec.sh targets 4 pools; with fewer, expected events scale down and the +24 h read says so (exposure_ready needs >= 8 expected). Opportunities per 20 bots per 6 h in the dry runs: 369-466.

exposure.note: Ready = the read window is >= 1440 min (NO KEEP before +24 h -- the +6 h read is mechanism and harm only) AND expected breaches at the control rate >= 8 AND the instrument (control climb rows and control opportunities) >= 1. Expected = control post rate x canary post opportunities.

own_lines.note: CORRECTNESS: 0 upward escape digs into water or lava by the canary -- _climb_flood_breach rows (a dig whose promise resolved, by the same live body, whose opened cell held water or lava 1.6 s later), excluding the submerged-water exemption. BLOCKS KEEP and triggers an investigation of each row; deliberately NOT evidence=defect (Codex r2): the row shows liquid in the cell later, not which action let it in, and mineflayer resolves a dig locally, so one row cannot license a REVERT on its own.
LIVENESS: canary-build _climb_flood_guard rows (restart-lag rows excluded). BLOCKS KEEP (INCONCLUSIVE).

POSITIVE CONTROL: control escape-climb rows (_scaffold_pick pillar_out/dig_straight_up) AND control climb opportunities are visible to this query (dry runs: 11,045 climb rows + 1,942 opportunities in 6 h; 40,065 + 6,603 in 24 h). BLOCKS KEEP.

EFFECT (design 4.1): observed canary breaches <= 2 (water entry within 5 min of a climb opportunity, the bot dry in the 60 s before). Decides only at the +24 h effect read with exposure (expected >= 8); a failure BLOCKS KEEP (INCONCLUSIVE), and an exposed failure is recorded as FLAT for the stopping rule (effect_flat). Not a KEEP threshold: zero observed.
HARM (design 4.1): stranded minutes per bot-hour ratio DiD <= +25% (trapped-bots definition: >= 10 min within 8 blocks with failure evidence). BLOCKS KEEP.
HARM (design 4.1): mining actions (mine skill rows + _ore_tunnel) per bot-hour ratio DiD >= -20%, so safety does not come from inactivity. BLOCKS KEEP.

primary.note: REPORTED (the decision is effect_ok + exposure): breaches per 100 opportunities DiD, expected vs observed, reduction; the two reported variants (entry within 8 blocks of the escape; the 72 h analysis's 20 s window); guard firings per 100 canary opportunities by caller and reason class; refusal-chain outcomes (out dry by ramp / stayed dry / later wet within 5 min); refusal rows and back-off; raw iron per bot-hour DiD; deaths by cause per arm.

harm.note: Unchanged: the two-death floor (OWNER 2026-09-11) and gather_ratio < 0.43 of control, from immobiledid. One canary death is reported and named, not a verdict. Stranded minutes and mining throughput are own lines above (they BLOCK KEEP; they cannot REVERT on a typed threshold).

teardown.note: THREE STEPS: drop-ins, clear canary_pool, restart the pool's bots 12 s apart; then confirm the live versions.

extension.note: Design 4.1: +6 h instrument and harm only; reads at +12 h and +18 h are harm reads (verdict NOT_YET before +24 h); the effect read is +24 h; if exposure is short at +24 h, ONE extension to +48 h, then INCONCLUSIVE (which under the stopping rule is not 'flat' but closes the loop).
